Sony Wireless Bluetooth In Ear Headphones: Noise Cancelling Sports Workout Ear Buds for Exercise and Running - Cordless, Sweatproof Sport Earphones, Built-In Microphone, EXTRA BASS –Black WF-SP700N/B I use active noise canceling (ANC) headphones all the time and prefer them to normal headphones as I tend to work in noisy environments and I’ve found that with ANC engaged I can play music at lower volumes. I like Sony headphones so I was excited to try these ANC ear buds. They’re a bit unusual in a few ways but they work well and are worth their asking price.

These are truly wireless and have no physical connection between them. Power them both on and they find one another. They pair via Bluetooth to a phone, tablet or PC, and the connection is stable up to about 40’ around corners. This is a good start.

There are several modes to these when it comes to the ANC function and each has its uses. I usually just use full ANC without any of the ambient sound modes turned on as it gives the best music experience. One of the two ambient modes is optimized for speech and voice, the other for more generalized noise. Neither completely cut off noise canceling, but rather they allow different bands of outside noise to come through. In full ANC mode, these are good noise cancellers, though not as aggressive as some others like Bose.

These have proven to be comfortable, and they have the little wings on each bud for keeping them in place in your ear. I used them while working in the yard and never once did I have a problem with slipping or falling out, even though I have the wrong size silicone insert on one of them.

The sound is very good but I would stop short of calling it outstanding. The bass is heavier than I like though not so bad that it gives me a headache unless I pump the volume up too much. The midrange is warm and full, and the highs are bright and crisp without being piercing. The sound can be adjusted a bit in the app that you can download, as it has an equalizer of sorts that lets you tweak the levels or choose a preset.

Ah, the app… This is the primary downside of these. The method to adjust these is either an Android or iOS app, not a physical piece of hardware and there is no Windows equivalent (for those who want to use these with a PC). The app is a little clunky though fairly self-explanatory and it does do what it’s supposed to do. Given a choice between an app or an additional piece of hardware, I would choose the hardware.

These charge up in the carrying case, which has leads that connect to each bud. Pay attention when you put these in the case – it is possible to reverse them, and while it hurts nothing the charging doesn’t work well… The case has some sort of battery in it and it charges the buds without being plugged in itself, though it does require occasional charging. Charging is fast – I charged them from empty to full in about an hour. One thing that could be improved, though: the buds can be popped in the charger while still powered on, and the act of charging them does not make them cut off. So, you can end up with dead buds and a dead charger too.

These are decent wireless sport buds that have good sound and good ANC functions. They’re comfortable and not overpriced. There are a couple of areas for improvement, particularly in charging but also in the app control, that would make these even better.
text_fidelity_b: Sony Wireless Bluetooth In Ear Headphones: Noise Cancelling Sports Workout Ear Buds for Exercise and Running - Cordless, Sweatproof Sport Earphones, Built-In Microphone, EXTRA BASS –Black WF-SP700N/B

SABRENT USB 3.1 Type-C to DisplayPort Adapter (DA-DPUC) If your PC or Mac has a Type-C port, you can use this SABRENT TYPE-C TO 2-PORT USB 3.0 AND HDMI ADAPTER (HB-HDUC) to add two high-speed USB 3.0 ports and an HDMI port. Note that an oval Type-C plug looks like a hollow lightning cable plug (see the illustration of the port and plug in the product page photo).

There are NO safe adapters available that convert a standard, rectangular USB Type-A plug to a Type-C plug, so you must have one of the still fairly uncommon Type-C ports to be able to use this hub. (The available Type-A to Type-C adapters do NOT meet industry specifications, and pose significant danger of starting fires.)

I’m a big fan of Sabrent products, because they’re affordably priced and always perform exactly as promised. This adapter is no exception.

text_fidelity_a:
Acer Aspire R 15 2-in-1 Laptop, 15.6" Full HD Touch, 7th Gen Intel Core i7, GeForce 940MX, 12GB DDR4, 256GB SSD, R5-571TG-7229 (WARNING- This is an in depth review of this laptop. My goal is to help those who are truly interested in making informed buying decisions. This is done from an experiential point of view of most consumers and not highly technical. If you prefer a shorter summary, see paragraph titled, THE BOTTOM LINE)

WHAT IS THIS LAPTOP LIKE?
I have had a lot of different tablets, laptops, desktops, and have built my own systems over the years. One thing I have not had is a hybrid laptop which changes from tablet to laptop and back again. I was not too fond of a 15 inch size as I tend to like smaller laptops, but I was willing to try. I am SO glad I did.

COVERING/CASE OF LAPTOP
This laptop is a thin profile, but feels very substantial. The bottom does not have tiny little rubber feet like some HP professional laptops I have had, but it has solid large rubberized pads that are 1 inch by a half inch. There are a decent amount of vents in the bottom as well. The top is a slightly textured metallic top (etched look) and not shiny. The hinges are very strong and hold the screen in a variety of directions solidly. They do not budge until I move them again.

SIZE
I am amazed that this is the first 15 inch laptop that I actually enjoy using! The size and way that it works makes it fantastic for me. I can tilt the screen in any direction and use my hands on the screen or keyboard in laptop mode which is a pleasure.

KEYBOARD
The keyboard is soft touch and rubberized key-wise. As soon as I touch the keys, a back light comes up so that I can see what I am doing. The back light goes out in 15 seconds or so when the keys are not being pressed. There is a full numerical keyboard and plenty of room between keys for my medium sized fingertips. It is also spaced well for those who have longer nails.

SCREEN
The screen is shiny. It doubles as a screen as well as touchscreen. The view on the screen is fabulous as it has a full HD 1080 resolution. The colors are not as intense as the Saumsung Galaxy Tab S2, which is one of the most amazing color screens I have worked with. Since I am a person who likes color, I like color intensity in my screens. However, this screen is fine and is by no means pale, it is just not quite as intense as I am used to.

TOUCHSCREEN
When you flip the keyboard back, the touchscreen clicks into place. You are given the option to choose the touchscreen if you want so there are no mistakes. As a tablet, I have found that it is very accurate and works quite well. I have put it through a lot and so far, I have only had a few instances where I was frustrated for a second, but it was easy to correct.

OPERATION
This turns on so fast it is almost jolting. My laptops, though usually professional level, often take quite a bit to boot up. This one, however is so quick it always surprises everyone here.

As for operations, I have found this to be a very fast and easy to use system. Load up is quick and the only problems I have from time to time are due to wireless and not really the fault of the laptop.

Turning it off sometimes makes me laugh out loud. Press button. BAM! It’s off.

WINDOWS 10
I am not a fan of Windows 10. But unfortunately that is pretty much the choice for any laptop at this point. This laptop seems to handle it very well.

GAMES
Because Windows 10 is not as game friendly as previous operating systems, I have not had the time to mess around with games with this. I have avoided Windows 10 until now, so I have not figured out what if any games will work with this. I will update when I do.

RUN TIME
Charging seems to take only a few hours for a full charge. The run time varies between 3 and 5 hours depending on what I am doing. I will say this- I rarely run it into the ground in one sitting, which makes it very helpful for me.

VIDEO
Runs very smooth on here. Using a DVD player means I have to use the USB port to run my independent unit and be in a stable position to do so. Works well. Beautiful to watch.

USB PORTS AND SD READER
I have found the USB ports to work very well. No problems to this point. Load up is fast. Using the SD reader is also a pleasure. The photos load up fast and due to the high resolution screen viewing them is really detailed and helpful. I have not installed professional graphics software yet to test this system for photo editing.

TOUCH PAD (AND FRUSTRATION)
The touch pad on this laptop is a bit challenging to use. There is a finger reader which I do not use, but the buttons are hidden in the pad itself and not two different buttons. The pad is pretty accurate as far as tracking. The only problem I have is location. When I rest my left hand on the rest area, sometimes it interferes with the touch pad and causes things to go a bit crazy at times. I am not pressing ON the touch pad, just in the area next to it.

SOUND
The sound is not tinny or awful. I find that it is sufficient for most of the applications I want to use it for. If I prefer to have a better sound, I use my Soundbot speaker and that gives me even better sound for movies and videos.

COMMENTS
I have to say that although the touch pad situation does frustrate me now and then, I do love this laptop. I have always wanted a hybrid because since I started using tablets, I would always catch myself touching the screen when I was using one of the household laptops and it was frustrating.

This unit is really nice. It is so fast and easy to use, it surprises me, honestly. It is so easy to switch between tablet and laptop modes and I find it a pleasure to work with for photos and movies.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This hybrid is VERY fast, easy to use, and boots up and shuts down so fast it is startling. The screen is a pleasure to look at, although not as color saturated as Samsung can be. So far, USB and SD works great. Sound is good enough for most applications. This is easy to use and not at all cumbersome. I love that I can touch the screen even in laptop mode if I am frustrated with the touch pad. I am very happy with this laptop/tablet hybrid.

RATING
FIVE STARS! I will update if I have anything else to add in the future, but at this point, I am very happy with this.
text_fidelity_b: Acer Aspire R 15 2-in-1 Laptop, 15.6" Full HD Touch, 7th Gen Intel Core i7, GeForce 940MX, 12GB DDR4, 256GB SSD, R5-571TG-7229

text_fidelity_a:
Nyne Boost Waterproof Portable Bluetooth Speakers with Premium Stereo Sound - IP67 Water & Dust Proof, 20 Hours Play-time, 100 ft Range, Built-in Power Bank and Mic, Loud Wireless Speaker,Grey Having outdoor safe speakers is essential for my household. Not only do I have audiophiles who are addicted to headphones and speakers, I have a husband who insists on taking his speakers to outdoor jobs. that is fine except when the job turns out to have a sudden rainstorm or high dust going on. Before giving it to him, I had our daughter put it through the grind at work (food prep) and in town events. Let's see how this speaker performs..

WHAT IS THIS SPEAKER LIKE?
This speaker is gray in color. The housing is very rubbery in consistency. The right side of the speaker has sealed controls under a rubberized pad over top of the buttons. The speaker stays put and is heavier than expected.

ON/OFF BUTTON/PAIRING
Holding down for over a second powers up the speaker. Next to the power button is the PAIRING button. This is not for pairing the speaker to a device but it is for pairing with another speaker just like it. A coworker with my daughter has this speaker and they tested it out- works GREAT so you now get two synced speakers.

CALLS BUTTON
You can send and receive calls with this button. You can also access your voice commands on your phone with this button.

VOLUME BUTTON
This is plus or minus sound controls. You can also skip by holding down- + is forward, - is backward.

PAUSE/PLAY
You can control pausing and playing with this button.

DOCKING
USB for charging, mini USB port (to use to charge a device if need be), and auxiliary outlet for like an old MP3 player or other device that does not have Bluetooth capability.

CHARGING INDICATOR LIGHT
Red when charging and turns white when fully charged. Will indicate when the power is running low so you will know.

SOUND QUALITY
Sound quality with this is very good. My daughter has a coworker with the same speaker so they both have had a chance to experiment with their speakers. So far it has been a great speaker. The balance of the recording of course affects the speaker, but so far it has not been overly muffled, out of balance, etc. Where you put the speaker affects how it sounds too.

When put on the floor, it really does sound better than on, say top of a box, or couch, etc. A very hard surface seems to really make it sound best.

VOLUME
When using the volume controls on the speaker, the sound is better than when you use the volume controls on the device (tablet, phone, etc).

DURABILITY
This speaker was taken to a huge town chicken and biscuit dinner and was dropped and still is working perfectly.

BATTERY
Two 10 hour shifts at full volume, and this speaker kicked through it all before needing to be recharged.

THE BOTTOM LINE
For a really nice durable speaker that is dustproof, shock proof, and supposedly water proof, this is a good choice. It is solid, has decent sound , and even can be synced with another speaker if you get two of these for coverage around a room.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. This is a decent speaker, and I feel more comfortable having my husband use this on his jobs than the other really nice speaker he was beating up.
text_fidelity_b: Nyne Boost Waterproof Portable Bluetooth Speakers with Premium Stereo Sound - IP67 Water & Dust Proof, 20 Hours Play-time, 100 ft Range, Built-in Power Bank and Mic, Loud Wireless Speaker,Grey

I ordered this kit to add more lighting options to my photography gear. My first impressions were that this kit is pretty complete in the sense that you get two lights with A/C power cords, stands for both lights, two shoe mounts and a decent carry case. With that said, I was not so impressed with overall quality of all included items. However, for all that you get in this kit, I am still quite impressed. Although this kit isn't of the best build quality it most definitely has great value with all that is included. The lights themselves are smaller than I had expected and the highest brightness setting isn't as bright as I hoped, yet it still has a place, and has come in handy many times to ad a bit more lighting to some of my projects.

I love that it includes the soft case and that the lights themselves have screens on the back that will actually show the color temperatures as well as the brightness level. I have more expensive lights that just have knobs on the back to adjust these settings with no easy way to know what color temperature you are at. This in-of-itself is a huge bonus as far as I am concerned. With this set I an easily select the exact color temp for each light to match. The stands are pretty basic. They are lightweight and easy to set up and take down. I am not so impressed with the quality of the Hot Shoe adapters as they are hard to solidly tighten the angle down without feeling like I am going to break the plastic knobs. They do function however, and I do appreciate that they included these, otherwise you would not be able to adjust the angle of the lights. The soft carrying case is decent and does have some padding if you don't throw out the included foam inserts.

Overall I find this kit to be effective, and have found that even though I may criticize many aspects of it, I do find myself using it quite often because of how convenient and easy to use and set up. There is most definitely value to this kit and I think that it would make a great lighting starter kit as well as a kit to ad more lighting options to your current lights. I hope that this was helpful.

However, my ears must be different because none of the different sized ear tips will stay in my ear when I am wearing them to walk or do yard work. I called asking if they have over the ear hooks/adapters to help keep them in place, and there are none.

I normally buy regular over the head earphones, and got these because of their noise cancelling properties and because they looked like they would be more comfortable. Our neighbors have a dog that barks all day long (literally) when they leave their home and I wanted peace and quiet when I go outside now that it is warming up and gardening season is here. Like I said, the noise cancelling works great. But, it only works as long as they stay in my ears, so I am using my husbands Bose OE2 headphones instead.

If my ears would hold the buds, I would LOVE these. They do work as promised. I am just disappointed there is no such thing as an over the ear clip accessory for those of us with ears that don't do well with them.

I called Bose and they are sending me another set of eartips to see if maybe these were just missized or defective.
text_fidelity_b: Bose QuietComfort 20 Acoustic Noise Cancelling Headphones, Samsung and Android Devices, Black

text_fidelity_a:
bopmen Headset with Microphone - Computer PC Headset with Boom Mic, in-line Volume Control & Mute, On Ear Wired Headphones for Skype, Home, Office, Classroom, Call Center, Black (S100) I got this for my teenaged son to use on his gaming PC. He had actually broken his previous gaming headphones and this seemed like a no-frills decent replacement for him to try.
The sound quality is actually quite good. Both the ear pieces and the microphone are crisp and clear, so no complaints there. However my son found it a little uncomfortable to wear compared to his larger over-the-ear style headphones before. The actual ear parts on this are smaller, which means they don't fully envelop your ears the way other ones do. On the plus side, this means it doesn't block as much external noise, which I like for him in our household (no more calling his name when he can't us!), but others may want more noise isolation. Also, the smaller ear pieces aren't as comfortable when worn as the larger ones.
I also didn't like that it didn't come with an adapter to break out for mic and speakers like other headsets do. I thought it would come with that as an option, as I've never gotten a PC headset that didn't offer either a splitter or TRRS combo adapter so you can use it with both a laptop that has mic/headphone combos as well as separate mic and headphone jacks commonly found on a desktop.
Thankfully I had an extra one lying around for him to use, so that wasn't an issue. But something to take into consideration. Others, I've got to give it at least 4 stars for working well and doing what it should. But there might be other options for the price worth considering as well if you want larger earphones or a breakout cable included.
text_fidelity_b: bopmen Headset with Microphone - Computer PC Headset with Boom Mic, in-line Volume Control & Mute, On Ear Wired Headphones for Skype, Home, Office, Classroom, Call Center, Black (S100)

TIANSHILI Wireless in Car Handsfree Speakerphones, Portable Bluetooth Speaker,Stereo Sound Enhanced Bass/Built-in Mic/TF Card Player/Google Assistant Voice Command for Car, Home, Outdoor After charging this device with the supplied micro-USB cable, I tried this as a Bluetooth speaker with my LG laptop. The sound was great. I also paired it with my boyfriend's iPhone and was able to answer a call by pressing the phone image on the speaker.

It supposedly connects to up to two phones simultaneously, but I did not have another phone to try it with. Also, there is a hands-free option but in order to use it, one would have to be playing music via a Bluetooth enabled in car device at the time a call was coming through or via the micro SD card. The rest of the time, when a call comes in, the phone button has to be pressed. This means it is not entirely hands free.

I did find that no matter what device I paired it with, that each device took time to find this speaker. The first pairing was the most difficult and I had to turn Bluetooth on and off several times and press the M button to wait until it registered. It took a while, but T826 is what it comes up as.

Besides the sound this small speaker generates, I like the removable magnetic clip on the back. It is easy to attach to a sun visor. There is also a slot for a micro SD card where an MP3/WMA audio file can be played from.

Overall, this is very functional. It has a lanyard for carrying that also makes it portable. The unit has to be charged every once in a while. The reason I got this is to use it as a portable Bluetooth speaker and not for answering calls.

IN THE PACKAGE
- speaker
- lanyard
- micro USB charging cable
- instructions

text_fidelity_a:
TRENDnet Wireless AC1750 Dual Band Gigabit Router with USB 3.0 Share Port, Pre-Encrypted, TEW-812DRU Let me preface this review by explaining that I work in the IT industry and support a variety of businesses with enough thorough experience in networking to say with certainty - the router I received is absolute garbage.

Now, normally I'd say for this price that you should set you expectations quite low - being in the field I'm in, I understand that almost all consumer routers are not great options, and the ones that are somewhat viable are on the $300+ range. Not everybody has the money or cares enough to invest this much - I get that.

So, that leaves me and my old roommate pretty much one option; the TRENDnet Wireless AC1750. He doesn't need much and especially doesn't want to spend much, it was tough getting him to go high enough in price to even this router- the old router he had came with his cable subscription 3 years ago. It worked fine but was sometimes slow with downloading over WiFi, not surprising. From the research and reviews, and most importantly the price - we decided to try this Trendnet AC1750 router.

WOW what garbage - he no longer gets WiFi in his bathroom corner of the house - it is a VERY small 2 bedroom apartment. How in the world can this router not handle a signal from 20 feet away, with only 2 walls in between? A router of this caliber (even at this price) should EASILY be able to handle covering a 2 bedroom small apartment. Period.

On to the second problem - even if we're connected, the WiFi signal drops constantly, I have to now reset this router every single day by unplugging it and plugging it back in because it refuses to work longer than 16 hours before crapping out. I have tried updating firmware, all network resets I can. I've even tried using the old modem (we replaced both router + modem) to see if that was the root of our problems - nope, it's the router.

It has slowly been getting worse and worse, and when I am gone from this apartment my roommate will be forced to reset his router every day, sometimes twice a day, just to get internet - or purchase a new one.

I am extremely dissatisfied with this product, although not quite surprised or disappointed given its price. It just seems odd that a 3 year old Netgear N300 router performs much better than an AC1750 Dual Band router.
text_fidelity_b: TRENDnet Wireless AC1750 Dual Band Gigabit Router with USB 3.0 Share Port, Pre-Encrypted, TEW-812DRU

text_fidelity_a:
Acer Chromebook 15, Intel Celeron N3350, 15.6" Full HD Touch, 4GB LPDDR4, 32GB Storage, Google Chrome, Pure Silver, CB515-1HT-C2AE, 15-15.99 Inches I ordered the Acer Chromebook 15, Intel Celeron N3350, 15.6" Full HD Touch, 4GB LPDDR4, 32GB Storage, Google Chrome, Pure Silver, CB515-1HT-C2AE, 15-15.99 inches so that I might have a lightweight portable travel laptop to enjoy and use for travel and at home. I have had some time with the new Chromebook and I would like to share a few thoughts and experiences with this particular model.

The first thing that I noticed with this Acer Chromebook was how thin and lightweight it was. It reminded me of a Macbook, though I have never owned one. I love the silver metal look and the keyboard is very enjoyable and comfortable to use. The speakers on either side of the keyboard are nice and sound amazing considering the size and the fact that they are housed in a very thin and compact space.

Initially I did experience some issues with the screen where it would not turn on despite the fact that there was power. It was very random but about 80% of the time the display would not turn on. I was able to contact Acer and they did resolve the issue within a reasonable amount of time. I had to send it back to Acer and they replaced the mainboard which I assume was the culprit. As I type up this review I am doing so on the repaired Chromebook and I have to say that though I had that initial experience, Acer made it right and I absolutely love this product! I’m not real savvy with the Chromebook OS but it really is simple and I appreciate the fact that this model comes with a Micro SD slot for my 128gb card which will come in handy to use for loading some movies and or music for on-the-go. Also it will come in handy for loading a few photos to edit with my favorite mobile photo editing app using the excellent touch screen which I quite enjoy.

Speaking of movies I have played a bit with Netflix, Google Movies and Hulu and the video quality is quite amazing with the 1080p screen resolution and, as I mentioned earlier, the sound is surprisingly loud and clear.

Battery life has been pretty impressive and lasts much better than I expected. As I stated before, this has been my first Chromebook experience so the only thing I have to compare battery life with is my much larger gaming laptop which I can't even get a few hours of use before I need to plug in.

Overall this Acer Chromebook 15 has been quite enjoyable, and because of Acer’s great support, I would highly recommend this Chromebook if you are looking for an inexpensive well rounded mobile “Laptop” experience.
text_fidelity_b: Acer Chromebook 15, Intel Celeron N3350, 15.6" Full HD Touch, 4GB LPDDR4, 32GB Storage, Google Chrome, Pure Silver, CB515-1HT-C2AE, 15-15.99 Inches

Targus Versavu Rotating Keyboard Case and Stand for iPad 2, 3, and 4, Black (THZ17101US) This polyurethane Targus Versavu Keyboard Case is beautiful, with imitation-leather exterior and suede-like "soft touch" interior. A hard shell (also with imitation-leather exterior) holds the iPad firmly in place, yet the iPad can be easily removed. The shell is attached at the circular hole shown in the product photos; the hole allows the Apple logo to show through. The shell rotates (with the iPad inserted) a full 360 degrees, so that the stand and keyboard can be used when the iPad is oriented either horizontally or vertically.

The lightweight keyboard is about the same size as the keyboard on my Toshiba netbook. The flat, non-contoured keys are reasonably comfortable to use. The keyboard is surrounded by a raised edge, to prevent scratches or damage to the iPad screen. The keyboard must be charged independently (using the included USB cable, attached to your computer). The keyboard will give a low-charge warning at 15% power, and shut down at 10% power.

This case (with cutouts for buttons, switches, rear camera, and charger plug) fits my iPad 2 perfectly, and the Bluetooth keyboard connects with my iPad 2. I didn't expect it to work, because the iPad 2 is equipped with Bluetooth 2.1 + EDR technology, while the iPad 3 is equipped with Bluetooth 4.0 technology, and the product description says that the case requires an iPad 3. The case does NOT have an automatic iPad Wake/Sleep switch that operates when you open the cover; however, the keyboard puts itself to sleep after 10 minutes of inactivity.

I like this case and all of its features, but it's not the "perfect" iPad 2 case. It adds weight and bulk, and apparently--judging from other reviewers' statements--the manufacturer recommends against using the case for anything but display (no carrying the case around in a backpack, tote, or bag). Because the keyboard works well, I rate it at 3.5 stars, rounded up to 4 stars.
text_fidelity_b: Targus Versavu Rotating Keyboard Case and Stand for iPad 2, 3, and 4, Black (THZ17101US)

Some are a major disappointment, but then there are those that are so well constructed and attractive that I forget about those others. The [[ASIN:B00D2CNXK2 Belkin 11-Inch Laptop /Chromebook Sleeve, Blue (B2B081-C01)]] is a beauty that I am very happy to have requested. Unfortunately, the dimensions are just as described and if your device is a hair over, there is no leeway because the outside gusset is not stretchy or flexible at all. You can't really tell from the images, but the opening of this sleeve is on one single end, that is the shorter side of the rectangle. Because the corners are all rounded, the zipper extends about an inch or two down the length, so you can wiggle your device in and out of the sleeve, provided it is not wider than 8 inches. Seriously. As I said, the black gusset is made of a woven heavy duty fabric, measuring about an inch in width, and there is piping sewn into both seams, front and back, for a finished appearance. A full sized pocket is sewn into the front of the sleeve and it contains a zipper as well. There is a small handle made of the same gusset fabric which is beautifully concealed when not being used. The neoprene is a lovely blue which is darker than the image online and I love it.

Because none of my devices can be squeezed into this sleeve, I am using it for other purposes. The price of this is perfect for a terrific sleeve.

Logitech M570 Wireless Trackball Mouse – Ergonomic Design with Sculpted Right-Hand Shape, Compatible with Apple Mac / Microsoft, USB Unifying Receiver, Dark Gray (Discontinued by Manufacturer) I prefer trackballs to mice and I have been looking for a good wireless trackball as my primary system is a laptop. In the past I had a Logitech TrackMan II, a hideous device that made my hands hurt. Logitech's new M570 trackball is far and away better than that TrackMan II, and I would consider it an excellent device except for one thing.

I have large hands, and as a consequence I need larger pointing devices to fit my hand. The M570 is marginally larger than my standard mouse which gave me pause right off the bat, but my concerns were unfounded. Even though this trackball device is not especially large, it fits my hand comfortably and I can spin the ball with ease without cramping my hands. My finger tips rest on the buttons and my thumb tip rests on the ball, while the fleshy part of my palm is on the desk past the plastic base. Finally, a trackball that fits my hand much like a normal mouse.

I have a marble mouse and while it's a decent trackball-like device, the ball easily drops out when the device is inverted and as a result I have dropped the ball one too many times and chipped it. The M570 holds the ball in place and does not allow it to simply come out without applying deliberate pressure, resulting in less opportunities to either lose or damage the ball.

The ball itself is a pretty shade of blue and, with the exception of the finger holes, looks a lot like a miniature bowling ball.

The M570 has 4 buttons and a scroll wheel that can be pressed for a total of 5 programmable buttons. The one problem with this trackball involves the scroll wheel - there is no horizontal scroll. While this is really just an inconvenience, horizontal scrolling has become very commonplace and that it is not included is a disappointment.

The range on the M570 us excellent. I am able to control the pointer on the screen from a distance of 15' - 20' away without any issues at all (except that it's harder to read the screen). This is very convenient and will be immeasurably helpful for presentations where the desk is a good distance from the computer and control is needed across that distance.

I am very pleased with the Logitech M570 wireless trackball and can heartily recommend it. The one improvement would be horizontal scrolling; otherwise, this trackball is superb.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech M570 Wireless Trackball Mouse – Ergonomic Design with Sculpted Right-Hand Shape, Compatible with Apple Mac / Microsoft, USB Unifying Receiver, Dark Gray (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

Mom and dad love them too, so we can’t really fault the two pre- teens from using and enjoying their electronics to the fullest. We like it best when they are at least devoting some of their electronic time to doing things more constructive and/or creative, and this is what convinced me to get my hands on this SOSUN Camcorder.

I had not heard of SOSUN until I got this camcorder, but I had read good things about the brand and decided that such a large percentage of customers must be right about something. One of my girls wanted a camcorder and this one seemed to have what she needed and seemed good for a beginner. The camera is lightweight and easy to hold. It can be used for regular picture taking and for video. The quality of video produced is good, too. There are better camcorders out there that create better videos and have more features, but this one is still good for a beginner like my 13 year old.

The battery life on this camcorder is about 2 hours. Given my kid’s short attention span, this is more than enough to keep her happy. In fact, she typically creates videos that are only two to five minutes in length. Unless her habits change, the 2 hour battery life is more than sufficient.

Camcorders can get expensive , especially if your needs and demands are high. But if you’re looking for a good starter camcorder for a very low price, this SOSUN is going to be difficult to match. The low price and above average quality make it worth the purchase and my increasingly more creative middle school age kid can vouch for its worthiness.

text_fidelity_a:
GorillaPod Video Tripod (Black/Blue) The Gorillapod Video Tripod (Black/Blue) is a good idea on paper but in real life it just doesn't quite measure up.

The pan & tilt head is incredibly stiff which leads to jerky motion and bounce in your video. There also, on mine at least, appears to be a good bit of free play or slack in the vertical movement of the control arm. I've tried to tighten this down to no avail. The mounting screw seems to be a bit long. It wasn't bad mounting my RCA Small Wonder video camera but when I mounted my Kodak still camera the screw bottomed out and left the camera loose on the mount. The mount itself seems quite secure tight and sturdily attached to the tripod.

I like the adjustability of the legs but if you're not using the tripod on a metal surface for the magnetic feet to cling to it tends to just slide around when adjusting the pan or tilt. The magnets do appear to be strong for their size and will hold my RCA Small Wonder video camera fully horizontal on the 'fridge or door of my car. I tried this with my Kodak Z-650 still camera and it was too heavy for the magnets to support.

While on the subject of the magnetic feet I wanted to add a warning that if you're using an older CRT style monitor care should be taken to keep this tripod several feet away from your monitor. Even being more than a foot away from my 19" CRT cause distortion and image warping. There is the potential for damage to CRT monitors.

As a stationary camera mount this is a pretty cute product; easy to carry, lightweight with near infinitely adjustable legs. If you just want to plop down your camera so you don't have to hold it this product works fine. When you bring the flaws of the pan and tilt features into play the enjoyment goes downhill fast.

All in all it's not bad but it really isn't great.
text_fidelity_b: GorillaPod Video Tripod (Black/Blue)

text_fidelity_a:
1MORE iBFree In-Ear Earphones Wireless Headphones with Bluetooth 4.2 AAC, IPX 6 Waterproof, Secure Fit, In-Line Mic for Sports Gym Running - New Model Black We blow through ear buds in our house and it seems that everyone has different ones that they like and don't like. Let's see how these measure up:

WHAT ARE THESE EAR BUDS LIKE?
These ear buds come in a nice box with a little instruction booklet. There is a little bag with three sets of gel caps in it. There are also three sets of hooks. Each of them comes in small medium and large. The hooks keep the buds in the ear but are soft so they don't hurt the ear at all.

The controls are on the right ear- the top hits about where the chin is. The connecting cord is big enough to be worn in front or back. The set comes with a cord but you have to have your own USB access to plug it into whether it be on an outlet or computer.

COMFORT
One of the most comfortable and secure earbud/headsets we have used to date- love that the hooks that help hold them in are soft so they don't hurt the ear, even after worn for a while.

PERFORMANCE
VOLUME
The headset gets the best result for us with the volume on max on the headset and halfway on the tablet that we use it with.

HIGHS/LOWS/MIDS
One of the things with this headset is that the highs are really nice and strong and so are the lows. The problem seems to be that the mids are drowned out making it feel like it is a bit out of balance. We have messed with it quite a bit and it seems to be the way it is.

SOUND PROOFING
These have excellent sound insulation capabilities. That does mean, however, that you need to be careful where you are wearing them if you need to hear what is around you or not.

BATTERY ALERT
When you first turn on the headphones, it will identify itself, tell you it is pairing and then give you an idea of how much battery life you have left- low, medium, or high.

POWER BUTTON
The power button is nice. Volume/skip functions are a challenge to get used to as compared to other Bluetooth headsets. There are sequences and timing as compared to others which seem to be simpler to use.

PAIRING
Very good pairing on all of the different devices we tested this with- several phones from Moto G3, Blu phone, Samsung Tablets and our stereo (forgot brand)

CHARGE
A charge has been lasting a good six to eight hours for us. Recharging seems to take us about three hours.

THE BOTTOM LINE
These are comfortable headphones that are easy to use, stay in the ears well, and have good insulation from ambient noise in the room or surroundings. They have nice highs and lows but tend to drown out the mids. The controls are a bit more challenging to learn at first as compared to other Bluetooth head sets we have used.

MY RATING
FOUR AND A HALF STARS- not able to give that so I am doing four. It is more like four and a half. The sound could be a little more balanced, and the controls not quite so difficult, but this is still a great set of headphones and we like it a lot.
text_fidelity_b: 1MORE iBFree In-Ear Earphones Wireless Headphones with Bluetooth 4.2 AAC, IPX 6 Waterproof, Secure Fit, In-Line Mic for Sports Gym Running - New Model Black

Grado Mini Adaptor I have a setup where I have some AKG-K701s running to a 30ft audio cable which connects to my receiver. This allows me to wander around the room while still listening to music without trouble - or almost without trouble. The headphones have a 1/4" stereo plug and the cable a 3.5mm jack, and though I tried two separate brass adapters (one of which was ASIN B01GPQJ5DA ) they were woefully inadequate for the task - loose from the very start, then constantly cutting out and eventually degrading entirely in the course of weeks.

This Grado adapter is in a completely different class. It was a nice hard snap, not only when plugging in the 1/4" connector but the 3.5mm as well. The short wire puts some distance between the two connections which relieves the stress. This is one case where the product is absolutely worth the price, I would recommend this to anyone who needs this kind of adapter.

EDIT: Six months later of kicking and dragging the adapter around the workshop has had zero effect on its performance. I've even tripped over it a couple times without issue. Still happy, still would recommend.
text_fidelity_b: Grado Mini Adaptor

The keyboard is good, but the mouse is huge. As near as I can tell, it is a 5000 series mouse. But it is HUGE. Does not fit my hand well, and the side buttons are small and not placed well. If it were on a system that was used for daily work, I would not recommend it.

11/11/2016
Update. The mouse, with VERY LITTLE use, is now erratic in behavior. Especially scrolling. It will actually scroll backward on a forward roll of the wheel until it seems to catch up with itself. Not what I would expect from a Microsoft product. But they don't make it, they just design it, and obviously don't care about quality control over their product in this instance. The mouse and receiver dongle are less than three feet apart. No excuse for any lag or miscommunication.

text_fidelity_a:
Nomodo U Wireless Wearable Bluetooth Speaker, Rechargeable and Portable I ordered the 'Nomodo U Wireless Wearable Bluetooth Speaker, Rechargeable and Portable' for review and would like to share some of my thoughts and experiences.
First off, out of the box this Bluetooth Wireless Speaker not only looks interesting but it is beautiful. I say interesting because I have never had a Wireless Speaker like this, and I wonder where would I use it and would it be practical. Well after some time with this device I must first report that it really does sound amazing. The sound is clean and immersive. It is hard to describe the incredible sound sensation while wearing it. It is almost as if you have speakers floating on either side of your head (pointing directly to your ears) and it is nothing like I have experienced before but it is pretty cool. I have been trying to think of how this Speaker would actually fit into my life. It's not like you are wearing headphones that only you can hear. While wearing this speaker, everyone else around you can hear it too but it's just not as immersive as it is to you. It's hard to describe, but what I will say is that it really is an incredible experience. If the volume is down low you can still hear your surroundings yet when you crank it up, surprisingly your surrounding sounds seem to disappear. Personally I have decided that this would be best worn while alone in your home while doing simple household chores. Like doing dishes or folding laundry. The Nomodo U speaker stays put pretty well for the most part due to the rubber neck pad, yet if you are constantly bending over or doing anything where you are moving around a lot and twisting your head and body, it tends to need re adjusted. Sitting in bed listening to Music or listening to an audio book works really well with this device as long as you wont be disturbing your partner. As for watching movies, for me this really doesn't work. I can't find anywhere where it says what version of Bluetooth this is using but I don't think it is Bluetooth 5.0 unfortunately. There are noticeable sync issues and this just gets annoying. Speaking of the Bluetooth, it connects/pairs effortlessly to all of my devices and that is a bonus. I am disappointed however that it uses Micro USB (the cable is included btw) for charging. With this being a new device it should have USB Type C. I always have to mention this with any new devices. Call quality is acceptable. Those on the other end can hear you just fine, as long as you are not in a loud environment. This is pretty typical with most wireless headphones. text_fidelity_a:
Logitech Performance MX Wireless Mouse (DISCONTINUED and Replaced by MX Master 2S) howdy y'all,

i bought this mouse to replace my logitech mx1100 cordless mouse. that one finally had the left mouse button start doing the dreaded false double click. it lasted several years, so i was not seriously annoyed. [*grin*]

for those coming from an mx1100, here are differences i noticed ...
- the mx1100 had the hump in the center instead of towards the back, so the main mouse buttons were shorter
this makes the mouse seem really rather too long. i am unsure if that will bother me once i use the new one for a while.

- the mx1100 had less of a slant to the right so that my hand sat a bit closer to level
the new one is more comfy for my very right-handed self.

- the mx1100 mouse wheel projected a tad more
combined with the sharp slant, the new mouse wheel feels like it is tilted the wrong way. it isn't, but i keep finding my finger on the right edge of the wheel instead of directly on the wheel.

- the mx1100 mouse wheel had a more pronounced side-move feel
the new mouse is very subtle. i liked the distinct feel of the older one when it toggled the side-move "button" function of the mouse wheel. of course, i like clicky keyboards, too ... [*grin*]

- the mx1100 had the upper thumb buttons just below the upper left edge
the new mouse has them on a surface that slants very sharply down to the left from the left edge. it makes the reach to the forward/back buttons a tad less comfy. combine that with a taper on those two buttons and i have found myself looking to see where the darned buttons went. they are also a tad more to the front of the mouse.
these admittedly annoying things that will likely fade out of my attention with use.

- the mx1100 used two AA rechargeable batteries
the new mouse uses one. since i use a lot of battery powered devices, i have a battery charger and several spares on hand. that means i will likely not use the usb charging function very often. still, one AA is better than having to charge two! [*grin*]

- the mx1100 had a larger usb wireless adapter
the new one is quite tiny! it works well - i put it on the back of my system among the tangle of wires that connect to other things and have had no reception problems.

*****
the parts list says there otta be a driver cd included. _not_ so! [*sigh ...*] you are referred to their download site if you want to use any of the extended functions or buttons. the performance mx has a $100 recommended price and there is no excuse to cheap out like that. thankfully, win7x32 has basic mouse support for the standard buttons, the mouse wheel, and the back/forward buttons.

this is a /_serious_/ fubar and i almost subtracted a star from my rating because of it.
*****

i suspect that folks with short hands will have problems with this mouse, but i am getting used to it already. i'm 6'1" and my hand is 7.5" from base to middle finger tip. not a _large_ hand, but not short.

*****
rated a THREE since it does what i expected - no more and no less. still, i came very close to rating this a two for not including the cd.

take care,
lee
text_fidelity_b: Logitech Performance MX Wireless Mouse (DISCONTINUED and Replaced by MX Master 2S)

text_fidelity_a:
Panasonic DMC-LX3 10.1MP Digital Camera with 24mm Wide Angle MEGA Optical Image Stabilized Zoom (Black) The wide angle lens is wonderful. The field of view and the speed (light gathering ability) of the lens can only be rivaled by high end camera and lens combinations costing six to ten times as much (admittedly those are superior in many other ways as well). Still, the point is that no other compact point and shoot camera can rival the field of view and speed of this one. Nevertheless, some things come up short of fair on the LX3.

The shutter lag is terrible. I am a very instinctive shooter that is quite capable in photojournalist style candids but I am almost always defeated by this camera.

I am not a photophile or electronic gadget spec sheet bench racer. I've done wonderful 8x10 prints with a 6MP camera and 10MP is enough to get prints after substantial cropping. I have huge film scans when I need them but I cannot realistically show dozens of megapixels on screen or in print for more than a handful of images. I also shoot in .jpg and it's great. I can't imagine the agony of terabytes of raw data jamming my PC.

I love the LX3 video quality for movies. It's ideal for Youtube and even Youtube HD. I do not like the Quicktime .MOV format or the weak compression algorithm. I wish it had H.264 and wrote an .MPG type format. It still beats the data format from a DVD camcorder though.

The audio quality for movies is terrible. Again, I'm not talking audiophile critique here. For comparison, my Sony DSC T9 (ultra compact point and shoot) has far better sound.

I hate the manual aspect ratio slider. If I shoot movies I want 16:9 but for stills I want 3:2 (of course). The LX3 requires that I remember to both turn the dial and slide the switch or I will end up shooting 16:9 stills.

Overall, it's a great camera. I hope they get the rest sorted out by the time I expect to buy another one in about 3 or 4 years.
text_fidelity_b: Panasonic DMC-LX3 10.1MP Digital Camera with 24mm Wide Angle MEGA Optical Image Stabilized Zoom (Black)

I have a few trips coming up and I'll test these on an airplane soon.

Headphone Adapter Converter Supports Audio and Charging for Motorola MotoZ, Letv ,2 in 1 USB-C to 3.5mm Audio Adapter, Nylon Braided 2 in 1 USB Type C Cable Fast Charge to 3.5mm Audio Jack(Black) I've been using a Keurig machine for several years -- I currently own 2 of them. But I've always had an ethical issue with all the little plastic cups that get tossed into the environment. To that end, I've tried and used several different varieties of reusable K-cups, and had finally settled on the Ekobrew cups.

I was offered an opportunity to try this set, and decided to do a side-by-side comparison. The results were interesting. These Brewooze cups perform just as good as the more expensive Ekobrew cups.

I tried several different coffees and several different grinds. As with all reusable cups, you have to be careful how fine/coarse the grind is. Too coarse, and you get weaker coffee; too fine, and you get either overflow and/or sludge. I found that a medium-fine grind worked best for both cup brands. This way, I get the right strength and almost no powdery sludge in the bottom of the cup. One advantage of the Brewooze over the Ekobrew: I was able to use LESS coffee in the cup to get the right brew strength. With the Ekobrew, I needed to fill the cup; with the Brewooze, I filled it about 2/3 full to get the same flavor/strength.

As with all reusable K-cups, you need to take care when you seal them prior to use. These are no trouble to seal correctly -- you can easily see if there are gaps and do an extra "squeeze." Inserting them into the machine takes a bit of attention, too -- otherwise, you can pierce the cup. There are arrows on the lid that show which direction, so that shouldn't be a problem.

This set comes with 20 paper filters plus a replacement charcoal filter for the Keurig filter wand. I didn't see much advantage to the paper filters except possibly ease of cleaning. The coffee was weaker, and using a finer grind didn't seem to help. And it still resulted in some grinds getting "around" the paper filter and onto the mesh, so I still had to clean the cup. It's not a big deal, really -- the cups are easy to rinse clean after use. So I won't be using the paper filters, but you may find them useful.

I'm a little surprised at how nicely these performed, given the price. You get 3 cups (brown, medium tan, and light tan color -- the photo makes them look orange, but they're more of a tan/brown), so if you want to assign a color to different family members, there you go. Since I usually brew 2 cups into a large mug, I just fill 2 of them with the same coffee and run them one after the other in the morning.

kI have to say I was impressed. I didn't expect these to perform as well as they did. Definitely comparable to the Ek​​​​obrew so far -- the only question I have is durability, and only time will tell. I've been using these for about 4 days, and after the initial side-by-side test (when I brewed about 12 cups total), I've been brewing 2-3 cups every morning, rotating them, cleaning after each use, and so far, no signs of any wear problems. If I notice a serious issue, I'll update this review.

Sample supplied for review; opinions expressed are based on my personal experience with this product.

text_fidelity_a:
Joymax 4MP Ultra HD Webcam with Microphone - 360-Degree Rotating Computer Camera for Work at Home Jobs - High Definition Web Cam for PC Laptop - Live Streaming Desktop Camera with Noise Cancellation A lot of these cheap webcams use very small sensors and rely on super wide optics to see the room. They also tend to overstate their resolving power, claiming to send a 1080 sized image that looks more like an upscaled 480. I'm happy to say this is a degree better than those!
The sensor is still small, as expected, but the optics aren't super wide to the point that edges distort. In fact, it seems pretty rectilinear (straight lines stay relatively straight in the background). The resolution seems decent as well. I'm not sure if it's actually resolved a full HD image like it claims, but it is definitely more resolution than a lot of the cheaper webcams I've tried. It looks pretty good and I'd argue that any live web call, skype, zoom, etc, will look perfectly fine with this camera and play at whatever resolution that protocol is capable of clearly.
The thing that sorta disappointed me, however, was the "ring light" built in. I mean, I have a REAL ring light so I get what that should do, but this sorta does... nothing. It doesn't create soft shadows or a circular catch light in my eyes- in fact, it's very hard to discern the difference between capture with the light on versus off. In a dark room, it can add a bit of illumination to the subject to make you a little easier to see, but it really isn't all that bright and under normal lighting conditions in my office, it makes zero difference at all. It also seems to get kind of warm as long as it is plugged in, even if not currently active, so I'm going to be in the habit of disconnecting it when not using, and only plugging it in when I need to make a video call at my desk.
For what it is, it is definitely a better webcam than most of the cheap ones, but it definitely is not perfect!
text_fidelity_b: Joymax 4MP Ultra HD Webcam with Microphone - 360-Degree Rotating Computer Camera for Work at Home Jobs - High Definition Web Cam for PC Laptop - Live Streaming Desktop Camera with Noise Cancellation

I will keep the mouse because it works well for what I need right now. But, Hey Kensington, consider a revised model that has room for the finger to rest somewhere on the right that does no result in a button press. Can't be the only one. text_fidelity_a:
Soundcore Wakey Bluetooth Speaker Powered by Anker with Alarm Clock, Stereo Sound, FM Radio, White Noise, QI Wireless Charger with 7.5W Charging for iPhone and 10W for Samsung I ordered the 'Soundcore Wakey Bluetooth Speaker Powered by Anker with Alarm Clock, Stereo Sound, FM Radio, White Noise, QI Wireless Charger with 7.5W Charging for iPhone and 10W for Samsung' for review and would like to share some of my thoughts after a few weeks.

First off, this thing is actually pretty amazing. The build quality is nice and aesthetically it looks clean. The sound quality is nice but not phenomenal. However for how small it is, it does produce decent sound and for a bedside alarm clock it does quite well. The wireless charging works great for my Galaxy Note 8 (and does in fact Fast-Charge) however there have been a couple nights to where my phone was not charged the next morning. The fast charger also works with my wireless earbuds which I attached an image showing the charge light on the Wakey, and the wireless earbuds case indicating charging. However for the wireless earbud charging, it does take some precise positioning to get them to charge. I noticed in other review that others weren't happy with the bright display light with no way to adjust it any dimmer than the lowest setting, however they must have updated that with a firmware update (which was super easy to do) as I had no issues with the display being too bright at night. I use the auto adjust setting which seems to work quite well as far as I can tell. Also I love the sleep mode sounds that you can adjust several (or just one) sound volumes to create your own personalized preference. I do wish that there were more sound options but the ones they provide are acceptable. I also wish that you could download and install more alarm sounds. Bluetooth connectivity is super quick and have never once had an issue with pairing it up to my phone. Really the ONLY issue I have with the Wakey is that to get the sleep mode sounds going, you need to connect with the app, and via Bluetooth connect to the device. No big deal right? Well my concern is that you will need to keep it connected for this feature to work. This means you will be connected to the Wakey ALL night and this kind of bugs me. It's just kind of creepy that the Wakey is connected to your phone all night while you sleep. I wish there was a way to just play your favorite white noise sleep sound by pressing a button on the Wakey device without having to always connect and stay connected to the app and your phone. The other gripe is that the plug design is huge and makes it so that I have had to move my nightstand further way from the wall to use it. Other than those two gripes, and the only reason for docking one star, the Soundcore Wakey is a very good product and a really great value.
*On a side note - I just tested the Wakey while watching some Youtube videos and the latency is not so good. There is quite a bit of delay and the voices do not sync up at all so I wouldn't recommend using the Wakey for listening to videos.
text_fidelity_b: Soundcore Wakey Bluetooth Speaker Powered by Anker with Alarm Clock, Stereo Sound, FM Radio, White Noise, QI Wireless Charger with 7.5W Charging for iPhone and 10W for Samsung

text_fidelity_a: TomTom GO Supreme 6” GPS Navigation Device with World Maps, Traffic and Speed Cam alerts thanks to TomTom Traffic, Updates via WiFi, Handsfree Calling, Click-and-Drive Mount You might think that with GPS on most cell phones these days you wouldn't need a standalone GPS, but this can still be very handy for navigation and gives you extras you don't get with a cell phone.  If you are making a long trip or driving in unfamiliar places, this is what you want.  The screen is nice and large; bigger than a typical cell phone screen.  If you have an older vehicle that doesn't have a Bluetooth connection to your cell phone, this Tom Tom has a feature to link to your phone so that you can talk on your phone through the Tom Tom; it is easy to set up and works well.  There is also a "find my car" feature, if you forget where you parked.  I haven't tested that yet, but it could come in handy.  This unit also contains walking directions, so that if you are trying to go somewhere on foot in an area you are not familiar with, the unit will guide you.  Some of the older Tom Toms had that feature; some did not.  If you have previously owned a Tom Tom, you will find the interface slightly different, but not complicated to figure out.  If you haven't had a Tom Tom before, you might manage to learn how to use the unit quicker than someone who has owned a previous model.  One thing that always bugged me with Tom Tom (and it is still in this version); you enter addresses backwards; you put in city and state first; then street name and direction and then street number last.  It works from the broadest part of the address down to the narrowest.  There are several pluses of this GPS over just a cell phone application, but I haven't had time to check them all out, such as real time traffic reports.  Also, if you plan to drive at all in Europe, Tom Tom seems to have better maps for Europe than other GPS competitors.  I don't know if this unit comes with world maps or just U.S. maps.  As far as accuracy, the device was off by about 1/2 block on my first destination.  It said that I had reached there, but wasn't quite there yet.  It's close enough so that most of the time you should be fine and maybe some destinations are harder to pinpoint than others.  I don't think you will be disappointed at all with this unit.  There is no power cord adapter, so you have to charge it through USB or in your car with the included adapter.  The older Tom Tom units had power plugs included for various countries (about 6 different ones I think).  With USB everywhere, I guess the need for an A/C adapter is not as important as it once was.  Almost a 5-star unit, but not quite there.
text_fidelity_b: TomTom GO Supreme 6” GPS Navigation Device with World Maps, Traffic and Speed Cam alerts thanks to TomTom Traffic, Updates via WiFi, Handsfree Calling, Click-and-Drive Mount

text_fidelity_a:
1MORE Quad Driver in-Ear Earphones Hi-Res High Fidelity Headphones Warm Bass, Spacious Reproduction, High Resolution, Mic in-Line Remote Smartphones/PC/Tablet - Silver/Gray I am not an audiophile by any means. I have Rockbox installed on my iPod video classic with a FiiO amp attached, all loaded with FLAC tunes. I listen to Spotify at work. That's the extent of my musical needs.
I have Audio-Technica headphones, and dream of some day owning custom Kaisers. That's my background.

I was pretty excited to get these. Right after ordering, I watched a few YouTube videos on them, and read up on Head-Fi. For the price, 1More seems to deliver outstanding products. Needless to say, I was pretty excited.

The box finally came and I was found to be very impressed with the presentation. You get a nice, magnetic box housing the IEMs, a leather(ette?) pouch, and multiple choices of ear piece tips. For starters, I found that the ear piece tips pre-attached to the IEMs were the most fitted for me, but I still do not find them perfect. They slide down a bit when in my ear, so there is some loss of sound. I will have to buy some aftermarket ones.

The microphone is also sub-par. This is the first time I've used a mic with headphones, and most of my calls could not catch my voice properly. I would get complaints that I sounded muffled or far away, and so I've resorted to using the phone mic most of the time. The mic buttons work flawlessly for playback features, however.

As for the sound, it's fantastic. With four drivers, I can hear so much more--and so many more flaws! I usually transfer music files into FLAC, and so I have pretty good sources for music. I've been using both my Samsung Galaxy S5 and Rockboxed iPod Video (equipped with a Fiio E11), and the sounds are great, but I'm noticing some files that weren't transferred correctly. I cannot connect to my computer speakers at work as the speakers do not have enough power to juice up the Quads, so be sure you have a more recent device or one with enough power to drive these IEMs.

I also use them on my Wii U's GamePad for Breath of the Wild, and they're actually better than my Audio-Technicas, even with the sliding ear tips. I hear a lot more, and sound is very important in the game.

All in all, amazing value for the price. The ear tip issue is more personal as my ears simply don't fit perfectly any of the ones provided, but I do wish the mic worked better.
text_fidelity_b: 1MORE Quad Driver in-Ear Earphones Hi-Res High Fidelity Headphones Warm Bass, Spacious Reproduction, High Resolution, Mic in-Line Remote Smartphones/PC/Tablet - Silver/Gray

text_fidelity_a:
Wiremold Cordmate Cable Management Box, CCBP8-WH,White I have reviewed several similar products and while this could work for some I found the design of this cable management box needs a bit of redesigning.

The point of cable management is to keep your cables looking neat and tidy - this can help achieve that - as long as your plugs are relatively small. While there are four rotating outlets on the ends they are close together and depending on the size of you power adapter plug many will block the plug next to it. I found this was also the case with the outlets located on the top.

This is nearly always an issue with power strips of any sort but when you try to add a cover this becomes even more challenging.

This brings me to the cover design. The side wings expand and must be spread to the maximum width in order to unlock and lift the lid - and even then it’s not easy. This inner cover is thin and not very substantial. Once the other wings cover it that is protected but access is difficult.

Typically I am a big fan of Legrand products and find their designs innovative, helpful and user centric. I cannot say that about this product after testing it for a while.

In real world use I simply have too may power adapter plugs and USB powered devices for this to be a viable solution at my desk. I found it works ok for my entertainment center though I already had my plugs organized there.

In the end, I would recommend one of the more simple box style cord management systems. These allow the greatest flexibility and are definitely far less frustrating to use.
text_fidelity_b: Wiremold Cordmate Cable Management Box, CCBP8-WH,White

text_fidelity_a:
Sennheiser HD 598 Over-Ear Headphones - Ivory If you're looking for closed headphones, the Sennheiser HD 598 Audiophile Headphones with High-Gloss Burl Wood Accents are NOT for you. On the other hand, the open back design of these headphones is perfect for my needs, providing clear and consistent sounds. With an open back headphone, you can hear outside sounds and what you're listening to can be heard by others around you. The sounds through these are clear and true, making them a great asset when listening to spoken word as for transcription purposes. Because they are so true, when hearing some older or poorly mixed tracks, the obvious difference in location recordings can often be jarring. I can get by that since these are wonderful when used in true stereo or hifi, well-mixed applications. They really do mimic a hifi speaker system in the small space of my head!

I'm not a fan of the burl-look in cars, and I'm also not crazy about the burl-look of these headphones or the beige band. Since I'm not looking at the headphones but rather listening through them, it's not an issue for me. The velour covered ear pads are thick, comfortable and have shown no signs wear since I've been using my set. I've spent many hours at a sitting listening through these and have yet to have a problem or complaint with the fit, feel, or sound. The band is rather easy to adjust, the pads tilt smoothly and once I've settled in, I've not needed to readjust unless I've removed the headphones.

I've used Sennheiser microphones in film and video production, both in the field and studio, having trusted them for providing great sound for a recording, but I've not used Sennheiser earphones until the HD598's in the Audiophile series. I wish my studio headphones were as comfortable as these, but then I'd need a closed set! With a long 10 foot cable, I'm able to move more than a couple steps and if I want to extend the distance, I can add on a longer cable. Coming with an attached gold plated phono (1/4") plug and a gold plated mini (1/8") adapter, I'm set for use on laptop, ipod, amplifier, television or professional equipment. I like them a lot and find that they improve every day!
text_fidelity_b: Sennheiser HD 598 Over-Ear Headphones - Ivory

This unit was meant to enhance the music sound quality from Alexa and expand our Alexa listening group and work with the living room television.

The speaker itself is considerably larger than my original Echo - wider and heavier. The lights on this are brighter as well - when playing music at night or listening to a book, you can leave the light on and it works as a night light. You can also turn the light off if you prefer. Setting this up takes a bit longer than my Echo or Dot - it's slower making the initial WiFi connection, but once you link to Amazon via the Alexa App, you're good to go. It connects via Bluetooth to both my LG V10 phone and my Samsung tablets without drama.

This unit is significantly louder at every volume setting than the original Echo and makes the Dot sound like she's whispering. I have this in our formal living room where we have 30 feet tall ceilings, grass cloth covered walls and an enormous open space - the room was designed for correct accoustics with my Grandmother's grand piano and music simply sounds beautiful in here. The Harman Kardon Alexa sits on a table where the piano used to be and the sound at volume 4 simply envelopes you no matter where you are in the room. Set the volume to 6 and I can hear my book or music two rooms away almost as if it's floating through the halls. The sound quality is excellent and playing Beethoven or opera or country music renders each instrument precisely from tiny flutes to cellos and twangy fiddles. I'm immensely pleased at the improvement from the Echo to this for just music.

The reason for the one star deduction is because I thought/expected the Harman Kardon to by fully, 100% integrated with Alexa. It is not. This unit cannot be linked to the Fire TV sticks, meaning that I cannot use it to verbally control the living room television. It cannot be linked to my Echo and Dot units. That means we can't include the Harman Kardon speaker in our multi room group so the same song/book can be heard throughout the house. We cannot do the Drop In skill where Alexa acts as an intercom system for multiple rooms. There are a couple of other skills this speaker isn't able to perform simply because it doesn't speak to the Amazon Alexa products. If they can correct this glaring deficiency, then this would be a five star product and one i would consider buying for the guest suite and master bedroom. As a stand alone Alexa unit, this is a top notch choice, but if you want to link to your existing Echo, you can't do so.
text_fidelity_b: Harman Kardon Allure Voice-Activated Home Speaker with Alexa, Black

text_fidelity_a:
JLab Rewind Wireless Retro Headphones | Bluetooth 4.2 | 12 Hours Playtime | Custom EQ3 Sound | Music Controls | Noise Isolation | with Microphone | Throwback 80s 90s Design | Black I wasn't expecting much given the price of this item, and I got pretty much what I expected.

The charging port is hard to reach and the LED charging indicator is difficult, if not impossible to see, without having to move the foam earpiece covering.

Setting up/pairing the device is pretty easy. Press the button for 4 seconds or so and you’ll hear a pleasant female voice say, “Hello”. This means the power is on. Continue holding the button and the device will enter pairing mode. You’ll hear the voice say, “Ready to pair.” When pairing is complete, you’ll hear the device say, “You’re connected” and tell you how much charge the battery has. So far, all I’ve heard is, “Battery full.” I have no idea what other battery indications the voice will give – perhaps only at 3/4, 1/2 and 1/4? Or maybe percentages?

The buttons are the biggest drawback with this device. Actually, it's really just one multi-function button on the right earpiece. The button functionality is not like any Bluetooth headset I've used before - very non-intuitive. The button has no label at all and the tactile feedback is nonexistent at times - I press the button sometimes and there's no "click" feeling. If a song is playing, it doesn't seem to matter where I press, the song stops if it is playing. When I press again, anywhere, it starts playing again.

There is no volume control on the headphones at all. You’ll have to adjust the volume from your phone/audio player. There is a bare bones EQ function. You control this by clicking the multi-function button 3 times in rapid succession. Each time you do this, the device advances to the next of 3 EQ setting – balanced, bass boost and JLab signature. The “balanced” setting seems to sound just like what it’s named – balanced or equal high, mid and low tones. The bass boos is decent – not overbearing. Not sure what the last one is, but if the pictograms in the manual are any indication, it boost the high and low ends. The EQ function does provide audible feedback – the voice announces each setting by name.

There's a next track function, but no function for going to the previous track. The next track function requires holding down the multi-function button for 2 seconds. There's no audible feedback for this function (other than a very short moment of silence). When you hear the silence, let go IMMEDIATELY. If you hold the button down for too long the Bluetooth connection will be severed and you'll have to reconnect.

Apparently, there's no ability to fast forward or rewind within a song or audio book. You'll have to do this on your phone/audio player. Pretty poor design if you ask me. BTW – I use this only with my audio player, so I did not test the phone/mic functions, but I’d be surprised if they were robust.

The instructions are minimal at best. The manual is one piece of paper printed on 2 sides. Unfolded, it's about the size of 2 business cards - about 4"x4.5" (10.16cm x 11.43cm). One side has instructions and the other is all promotions/disclaimers, etc. That's it.

Sound quality is acceptable - decent bass and stereo separation is good. I’m no audiophile though. The product description says it has "Noise Isolation", which is marketing speak used by all on-ear headphone manufacturers. It simply means the ambient noise is slightly reduced because the headphones cover your ears. Bottom line - there's no tech/function in this device that does any active noise cancellation.

The headphones are a little snug/tight, but not so much to be uncomfortable - at least that's my opinion after an hour+ of testing. Not sure if this will be true for something like a 3-4 hour flight. I’ll test this out in the near future and will update this review, if possible.

The charging cable that comes with the item is 9” long (22.86cm). Not very useful at all, but better than nothing.

On the plus side, the manufacturer did provide an extra set of foam earpiece covers - the set that comes on the headphones is orange. The extra set is black.

Bottom line, for $15 I wasn't expecting a lot - well maybe better button functionality, but hey, what can you do? As my granddad used to say, “You pays your money and you takes your chances.”
text_fidelity_b: JLab Rewind Wireless Retro Headphones | Bluetooth 4.2 | 12 Hours Playtime | Custom EQ3 Sound | Music Controls | Noise Isolation | with Microphone | Throwback 80s 90s Design | Black

text_fidelity_a:
Nikon AF-S DX NIKKOR 55-300mm f/4.5-5.6G ED Vibration Reduction Zoom Lens with Auto Focus for Nikon DSLR Cameras This is my current go-to lens. I wish I could afford one of the more fancy-schmancy professional telephotos, but until then, this one is the one parked on my Nikon D7000.

Uses:

1. Birds, bugs and other critters from a safe distance or on the fly/run
2. Portraits of one or two people (gives excellent bokeh)
3. Landscapes and seascapes, especially in vertical/portrait mode.

Limitations:

1. Buildings from across-the-street distance
2. Large groups of people
3. Macro shots from thisclose

Depending on the type of photography you enjoy, this may or may not be the lens for you. It works fine for me for the uses above, especially when the subjects are a respectable distance away, but it doesn't have a wide enough angle for limitations 1 and 2, and if you're closer than a couple of feet it won't focus properly.

It's also pretty heavy, but makes up for this by making you look like a pro who knows what they're about, especially when you use the lens hood (included and highly recommended for use)

The auto-focus is not as smooth as it should be, and you can sometimes hear the mechanism moving around trying to do its job, but image stabilization and the tripod detection mode are huge pluses. (It also attaches/detaches from the camera in the opposite direction to my other (Sigma) lens)

For the type of photography I'm doing at the moment. even if it's not on the camera, this lens goes with me wherever I roam.

Amanda Richards, March 30, 2012
text_fidelity_b: Nikon AF-S DX NIKKOR 55-300mm f/4.5-5.6G ED Vibration Reduction Zoom Lens with Auto Focus for Nikon DSLR Cameras

This is a rear view monitor only - not a dashcam - and it works far better than one of the combination rear monitors/dashcams that I have also used.

Since there are a large number of reviews that cover this in detail I am going to keep mine brief. Here is the single thing I do not like about it: the terrible documentation. On the other hand you can have this professionally installed for not a lot of money, which is the route that I took. If you are a do-it-yourselfer installing it right is less than an hour job (according to the tech who installed mine).

What I love is the clear visual behind me. The camera works in dark and low light, and the display has sufficient clarity and resolution to easily see what is behind you and estimate distances. If you were to purchase this as an option on a vehicle I shudder to think of the cost, but for less than one hundred fifty bucks professionally installed this is a bargain. And if you do install it yourself you can knock a C-note off that cost.

If you parallel park frequently this is a perfect way to make that easier. For rural driving this may not be a needed accessory, but for city use it's a convenience (and a safety feature as well.) Do note the information in the product specs too because they are clear about what this will and will not work with.
